problem: Prior foundation-model work on quadruped robots only handles planar scenes and does not exploit 3D terrain crossing (stairs, ramps, gaps, doors); VLMs lack 3D grounding and memory, and existing sim-to-real locomotion policies (RMA, teacher-student imitation) lose performance when deployed.
motivation: Quadruped robots could traverse complex 3D terrain, but system-level autonomy is lacking. VLM common sense could fill the data gap, but ego-view 2D images must be turned into 3D interactions, and locomotion must be robust with proprioception only.
key_idea: Use a zero-shot VLM (LLaVA-34B) to decompose terrain-crossing into (Action, Ending) sub-tasks, execute them in a VLM double-checked closed loop with depth/VIO-based sub-goals, and drive a blind RL locomotion policy trained with Probability Annealing Selection (PAS).
insight: Closed-loop sub-task execution with VLM double-check is crucial: without it, real-world overall success drops to 10-20% versus 25-60% for the full system. Overall success is bounded mainly by VIO localization (stable-localization rate is 63-94%), since blurry images from dynamic motion cause errors. For locomotion, gradually annealing from oracle latents to predicted latents (exp 0.9998) beats pure imitation (RMA, IL) and blind/concurrent training, since RL reward feedback is retained.
method: Task decomposition: prompt the VLM on the ego-view RGB and instruction to identify the intermediation (stair/ramp/gap/door) and output a sequence of (Action in {move, climb}, Ending in {facing, across, to goal}) sub-tasks

Closed-loop sub-task execution: a VLM discriminator judges whether each sub-task ended; the next one starts only when both the workflow and the VLM signal completion (double-check), with repeated adjustments such as center alignment

Perception-to-3D sub-goals: the VLM outputs an intermediation bounding box, which is back-projected with aligned depth into a 3D sub-goal; VINS-Fusion VIO provides odometry, and PD control produces velocity commands
Oracle policy training: PPO in IsaacGym with proprioception (45), privileged state (4) and terrain heights (187), the latter encoded to a 32-d latent, over an 8-category terrain curriculum

PAS partial-observation training: an LSTM+MLP estimator predicts the latent from proprioception alone; the actor input is the real latent with probability alpha^iteration and the predicted latent otherwise, annealed to fully predicted, with RL loss optimizing both
Terrain classifier: a frozen-policy head with BCE loss classifies plane vs on-intermediation and signals the end of 'climb across' when the terrain changes back to plane

setting.backbone: LLaVA-34B (frozen, zero-shot) for high-level reasoning; PPO-trained MLP/LSTM locomotion policy (PAS) from scratch
setting.training_data: VLM: none (zero-shot). Locomotion policy: RL in IsaacGym, 4096 agents, 2x40k PPO iterations, 80-terrain curriculum. No demonstrations.
setting.observation: ego-view RGB-D (RealSense D435i, 848x480) + stereo images for VIO + proprioception
setting.action_space: VLM sub-tasks -> velocity commands (Vx,Vy,Vyaw) -> 12 joint position targets with PD control at 50 Hz
setting.simulator: IsaacGym (locomotion training only); high-level evaluated in the real world
setting.privileged: none at test time for locomotion (blind, proprioception only); the goal position (x,y,z,yaw) relative to the start and a language description are given

numbers.extra: real Unitree A1; VIO localization; goal pose given
numbers.evidence: Table 1: Stair row, Overall 60%, Stable Loc 88%, w/o Closed-Loop 10%, Across Terrains 70%

numbers_note: No standard VLN/ObjNav benchmarks; results are custom real-world trials. Real-world locomotion SRs (Table 3): PAS stair 100, ramp 90, rubble 95, grassland 100, unseen obstacle 95.
results: On real-world crossing of stairs, ramps, gaps and doors, SARO gets 60/25/45/30% overall success (70/50/80/50% counting only terrain crossing), while ViNT and the LSTM baseline get 0% everywhere and NoMaD gets 0-20% except 70% on doors. PAS reaches 85.31% average simulated success versus 77.34% for the blind policy, the strongest baseline, and beats RMA and IL in real-world trials.
limitations: Overall success is limited by VIO localization, which is unstable under high-frequency vibration and motion blur
Only short, simple single-intermediation tasks with ego-view perception and no memory
Small evaluation (20 trials per terrain), custom baselines and setup; needs a GPU server for the VLM
builds_on: Legged gym terrain curriculum (Rudin et al.)
